Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan for #9863: stop the conflict resolver from retrying a refused Claude fallback (exit 76)

Planning ref: `8ef44d82d4f2cabd25bd0ac335c904c646f765be` (branch `main`). The integration branch mismatch line reads `unknown`, not `true`, so planning goes ahead.

Clarification answers (AD-1, unblock judge):
- **Q1: A.** Make the exit-76 hardening under this issue, in the conflict resolver script, with a regression test. The heal scope has to be widened by the pipeline (a pipeline grant or a replacement heal issue). Hand edits do not count.
- **Q2: B.** The Claude pool problem is not confirmed fixed. This plan states that the hardening alone does not turn `review / codex-agent` green. Refreshing the pool is an operator step outside this repository.

### Automation / scheduling (§20.E)
- This only changes existing code. No new script, scheduler entry, supervisor or database work, and no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry.
- The change runs where it already runs: `review_autofix.yml`, step "Run Codex resolver, validate, stage, commit". No workflow file changes, so workflow size (§24) and runner concurrency (§26) are not affected.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`
- `tests/test_review_autofix_claude_fixer_mode.py`
- `changelog.d/9863-resolver-refused-fallback-no-retry.md` (new)

## Deferred scope
- The review / codex-agent job stays red until the Claude account pool yields an account again, which needs the operator token refresh through the claude-workers key-sync workflow or a re-run after a transient broker outage.

## Acceptance
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_review_autofix_claude_fixer_mode.py::test_resolver_claude_refused_fallback_is_terminal red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_review_autofix_claude_fixer_mode.py::test_resolver_claude_refused_fallback_branch_contract red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_review_autofix_claude_fixer_mode.py::test_resolver_claude_isolation_failures_never_call_host
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_review_sandbox_claude_roles.py::test_claude_resolver_isolation_failures_do_not_select_host_writer
ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: the resolver path only runs inside pull-request review runs, and that job stays red until the Claude pool yields an account

## Functions or modules to implement

**1. `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`: the Claude branch of the attempt loop (around lines 4000-4035 on this ref)**

Add one block right after the existing exit-80 block (lines 4014-4021) and before the `if [ "${resolver_claude_rc}" -eq 75 ]; then` hand-off to OpenCode. It runs when `resolver_claude_rc` is 76. It copies the shape of the exit-80 block:
- Find the refusal reason with the helper in item 2, then log one line to stderr:
  `Conflict resolver: Claude unavailable (refused fallback reason=<reason>); not retrying.`
  The line must not contain the text `AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK role=CONFLICT_RESOLVER`. The existing test `test_claude_resolver_isolation_failures_do_not_select_host_writer` requires that string to appear only once in the branch.
- Call `emit_conflict_resolver_substate "Failed" "${attempt:-0}"`.
- Remove `${tmp_output}` when it is set, the same way the exit-80 block does.
- Set `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_EXIT_CLASS="other"` and `exit 1`.

Effects:
- No second sandbox is built and the loop does not retry.
- The OpenCode attempt never runs. Today it doesn't run on 76 either: line 4036 only calls it on 75.
- `opencode_emit_failure_alert … invocation_failed` (line 4225) is never reached, so the failure is no longer blamed on `MODEL_EDITOR`.
- The final exit code (1) and terminal class (`other`) match what today's third attempt produces at lines 4236-4238. Downstream handling is unchanged: `finalize_reason=conflict_resolver_failed`, the `RESOLVER_TERMINAL` record, and failure markers. Only the attempt count drops from 3 to 1.

Short comment to put in the code: 76 means `ai_engine_fallback` refused a non-capacity fallback (plan item 3e, D1). The result is the same on every retry, and the resolver must never run codex in its place.

**2. `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`: new helper `_resolver_refused_fallback_reason`**

Put it next to `_resolver_fail_closed`. Check the name is not already used in the file (§10).
- Records file: `${AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK_RECORDS_FILE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/ai-engine-fallback-records.tsv}`. This is the same default `ai_engine_fallback` uses (`scripts/ai_engine.sh:287`).
- Print `unknown` if the file is a symlink, is not a regular file, or cannot be read.
- Otherwise read only the last 50 lines with `tail`. Take the last `v1` record where field 3 is `CONFLICT_RESOLVER` and field 6 is `refused`, and use field 4.
- Print that value only if it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,60}$`; otherwise print `unknown`.
- Always return 0 and never stop the script on failure, even under `set -e`.

### Data structures affected
- None changed. The helper only reads the existing TSV record (`v1`, ts, role, reason, class, action, policy) that `ai_engine_fallback` writes.

### API or interface changes
- No new environment variables, labels, outputs or `GITHUB_ENV` writes.
- `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_REASON` is not set on this path, same as today.
- Exit code and terminal class are unchanged. Only the attempt count and log wording change.
- The new line has no `KEY=` prefix, so it is not a stable log prefix and needs no `agents.d/` fragment.

**3. `tests/test_review_autofix_claude_fixer_mode.py`**

Reuse the existing harness: `FAKE_SANDBOX`, `_resolver_claude_sections` and `_run_resolver_claude_section`. That harness runs the real call-site code.
- Add `_resolver_refused_fallback_reason` to the list of functions `_resolver_claude_sections` extracts.
- Add a `FAKE_SANDBOX` `run` mode, `claude_refused`. When `$7` is `claude`, it appends the record body from `${REFUSED_RECORD}` (default `CONFLICT_RESOLVER\tno_credential\tnon_capacity\trefused\tcapacity`) to `${AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK_RECORDS_FILE}` as a `v1` record, then exits 76. When `$7` is `codex`, it writes output as if it succeeded, so a wrong fallback would be visible.
- `_run_resolver_claude_section` gets optional `records`/`env` overrides. Point `AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK_RECORDS_FILE` at a file under `tmp`. Add `trap 'printf "terminal_class=%s\n" "${RESOLVER_TERMINAL_EXIT_CLASS:-unset}"' EXIT` to the generated script. That only adds stdout, and existing tests only assert `codex_exit=0`.

New test `test_resolver_claude_refused_fallback_is_terminal` (fails on the current base, where the section falls through with `codex_exit=76` and rc 0). Parametrized cases:
- a valid `no_credential` record
- a missing records file
- a records-file symlink
- a reason with unsafe characters
- a newer record whose role is not `CONFLICT_RESOLVER`

Assertions:
- rc is 1 and stdout has `terminal_class=other`.
- Exactly one `prepare-ephemeral` call and one `run|claude|CONFLICT_RESOLVER|write|…` call.
- No `run|codex` call and no `host` file.
- stderr has `refused fallback reason=no_credential); not retrying.` (or `reason=unknown` for the bad-input cases).
- Neither output contains `invocation_failed` or `openai/gpt-6-sol`, and stdout has no `codex_exit=`.

New test `test_resolver_claude_refused_fallback_branch_contract` (a static check):
- In the `resolver_claude_rc=75` … `resolver_clean_output=` branch, the `-eq 76` block comes after `_resolver_sandbox_attempt claude` and before the `-eq 75` OpenCode hand-off.
- The block contains `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_EXIT_CLASS="other"` and `exit 1`.
- The block does not contain `opencode_emit_failure_alert` or `_resolver_sandbox_attempt codex`.
- The existing exit-80 block is unchanged.

**4. `changelog.d/9863-resolver-refused-fallback-no-retry.md`**: one fragment describing the behaviour change, with a non-closing reference only.

## Decisions

### D1 — Where exit 76 becomes terminal
- Chosen: in the Claude branch, right after `_resolver_sandbox_attempt claude`, copying the existing exit-80 block.
- Alternatives considered: a `76)` arm in the generic non-zero-exit `case` (lines 4193-4211), as the issue suggested; or passing `claude` as the engine to the OpenCode alert.
- Why: 76 only means "refused" when the Claude sandbox returns it through `ai_engine_fallback`. The generic `case` also handles OpenCode/codex exits. Stopping in the Claude branch also skips the misleading `invocation_failed` alert and the "OpenCode non-zero exit" text, and it reuses a pattern the branch already has.

### D2 — Where the logged reason comes from
- Chosen: the last `CONFLICT_RESOLVER`/`refused` record in the fallback records file, checked against an allowed-character pattern, or `unknown`.
- Alternatives considered: `AI_ENGINE_LAST_FALLBACK_REASON`, or no reason at all.
- Why: the sandbox runs as a child `bash` process (line 1093), so the variable it sets never reaches the resolver. The resolver also does not source `scripts/ai_engine.sh`. The records file is the persisted channel the job's report step already reads.

### D3 — Keep policy, exit class and failure reason as they are
- Chosen: exit 1 with class `other`. No new `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_REASON`, no codex fallback, and no change to the fallback policy or the pool step.
- Alternatives considered: a new `conflict_resolver_claude_refused` failure reason; falling back to codex on `no_credential`.
- Why: the refused fallback is a deliberate security control (§6). A new failure reason would change heal routing and fingerprints, which is out of scope. Keeping the same exit behaviour keeps downstream contracts unchanged (§10, §18).

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundary:** the records file under `RUNNER_TEMP` is written by host helpers in the same job. It is still read as untrusted input: symlinks are refused, only the last 50 lines are read, and the reason must match `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,60}` before it is logged. Nothing read from the file is executed.
